originalTitle: Trump downplays war with Iran, in which 18 US service members have been killed so far, as ‘small potatoes’ – live
summary: Thousands of Iranians have been killed and more than 750 US service members have been wounded during the ongoing conflict
content: Around 50 members of the military’s Joint Staff have been subject to polygraph tests, according to a report by the New York Times. The tests were reportedly part of the Pentagon’s goal to weed out personnel leaking sensitive information to the press. Some of the people required to take the polygraph tests were high-ranking officials, according to CBS News, including officials in Central Command and other combatant commanders. The polygraph tests reportedly came after several publications described diminishing stock pile munitions, such as Patriot interceptors and long-range missiles, in their reporting. Pete Hegseth, secretary of the Department of Defense, has sought to crackdown on leaks to the media. In July, he announced a joint task force to investigate leaks and identify those behind them. And as far back as March 2025, Hegseth warned that investigations into leakers would involve polygraph tests. The sheer number of people reported to have taken the tests is rare for the Pentagon, which uses polygraph tests but not in large swaths. Donald Trump’s “Build the Wall” game is getting blowback from the game maker Tetris. The game, which is a near replica to the iconic falling blocks game, has the player build a structure to “protect the border from the coming horde.” In a post on X, Tetris wrote that: “we take copyright infringement very seriously.” The company added that it was not involved in the creation of the administration’s game and said, “at Tetris we believe in the power of connection and bringing people together, not dividing them”. The White House launched an “arcade” on Thursday, that houses five 80s-style computer games that includes “Build the Wall”. Other games involve the player flying a bald eagle down the National Mall and acting as border patrol agent along the Rio Grande river. Adam Telle said Friday that he is “honored” Donald Trump named him as the acting army secretary to replace Daniel Driscoll. He comes to the role, which is the army’s top civilian post, after serving as the assistant secretary of the army for civil works. “My previous work in the Army focused on moving at Trump Speed to deliver on one of the Army’s original missions,” Telle wrote in a post on X. “I will apply that same relentless focus on efficiency to how the Army mans, trains, equips, and modernizes.” Driscoll’s departure came after widespread reports of tensions with defense secretary Pete Hegseth. Driscoll gave no reason for leaving, but reportedly clashed with Hegseth after some of his allies had been ousted by Hegseth. Telle said Hegseth’s leadership at the department of defense is “historic” and that working closely with the department “we will deliver a more ready and capable Army”. On Truth Social, Trump called Telle: “A Great Patriot, who is respected by all.” Donald Trump’s executive order to limit mail-in voting has been blocked again by a federal judge. US District Court Judge Indira Talwani initially placed a temporary order blocking Trump’s mandate and has now replaced that with a stronger preliminary injunction. “Plaintiff States are required under state law to mail millions of ballots to voters on a prescribed timeframe. As detailed below, they are unable to pivot this late in the election cycle, nearly guaranteeing significant disenfranchisement for eligible voters,” the judge wrote in her ruling. Her injunction comes after Trump signed an executive order in March that would create a nationwide list of verified eligible voters and compel the US Postal Service (USPS) to work with states to establish lists of mail-in voters before elections. This would mean a limited ballot delivery only to voters on those lists. USPS has said in recent court filings that the technology needed to administer the order isn’t even available. Earlier this week, a USPS whistleblower came forward and warned of “potentially catastrophic problems” if the agency were to try and carry out the order. After Trump signed the order, a coalition of 24 state attorneys general joined together suing USPS to challenge the rule. They also filed a motion for the temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction as litigation was ongoing. Oral argument on the coalition’s request for a preliminary injunction was held on Thursday. “We’ve now secured longer-term relief that will keep the USPS changes blocked while our case moves forward,” said Rob Bonta, the attorney general of California, which co-led the state coalition. “We will continue to take all steps to stop the Trump Administration from trampling on voting rights and restricting mail voting.” Donald Trump told reporters in the Oval Office on Friday that his real estate background has helped guide his knowledge on data centers. He said that if he were in charge of a city or state, he’d try to get in as many data centers as possible. “If you want your house to be more valuable and everything else, you’re going to want a data center,” Trump said. “If you want to go through poverty, crime, and squalor, I would say don’t approve data centers, you know, you have your choice.” The president’s remarks come as a nationwide backlash to data centers is underway, which is likely to be a flashpoint for the midterm elections. Town meetings have filled with constituents angry about massive data centers moving into residential neighborhoods and small towns. They worry about pollution, loud humming noise and strains on the electrical grid and water supply. The momentum has even caused some notable republicans, like Texas Governor Greg Abbot and Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, to regulate data centers. While speaking with reporters on Friday, Trump said that he’s letting companies build their own power plants so they don’t have to use the grid, which would mean lower energy costs for residents. chineseTitle: 特朗普淡化与伊朗的战争，迄今为止已有 18 名美国军人丧生，称其为“小人物”——直播
chineseSummary: 在持续的冲突中，数千名伊朗人被杀，超过 750 名美国军人受伤
chineseContent: 据《纽约时报》报道，大约 50 名军方联合参谋部成员接受了测谎仪测试。据报道，这些测试是五角大楼清除向媒体泄露敏感信息的人员目标的一部分。据哥伦比亚广播公司新闻报道，一些被要求接受测谎仪测试的人是高级官员，其中包括中央司令部和其他作战指挥官的官员。据报道，测谎仪测试是在几份出版物在报告中描述爱国者拦截弹和远程导弹等弹药库存减少之后进行的。国防部长皮特·赫格斯 (Pete Hegseth) 一直在寻求打击向媒体泄密的行为。 7月，他宣布成立联合工作组来调查泄密事件并查明幕后黑手。早在 2025 年 3 月，赫格斯就警告称，对泄密者的调查将涉及测谎仪测试。据报道，参加测试的人数对于五角大楼来说是罕见的，五角大楼使用测谎仪进行测试，但规模并不大。唐纳德·特朗普的“筑墙”游戏遭到游戏开发商俄罗斯方块的反击。这款游戏几乎是标志性的落块游戏的复制品，玩家需要建造一个结构来“保护边界免受即将到来的部落的侵害”。在 X 上的一篇帖子中，俄罗斯方块写道：“我们非常严肃地对待版权侵权行为。”该公司补充说，它没有参与政府游戏的创建，并表示，“在俄罗斯方块，我们相信联系的力量，并将人们聚集在一起，而不是分裂他们”。白宫周四推出了一个“街机”，里面有五款 80 年代风格的电脑游戏，其中包括“Build the Wall”。其他游戏涉及玩家驾驶秃鹰飞过国家广场并充当边境巡逻人员
